ZERO REPORT – 10 DEC 2025
WEST COAST + ASIA HYDRO-SEISMIC FRONT

PACIFIC NORTHWEST
– Cat 4/5 atmospheric river slamming WA.
– NWS expecting catastrophic flooding risk on Skagit/Snohomish, major flooding along western Cascade foothills, plus landslides in steep terrain.
– Mount Rainier forecast: ~110”+ snow at 14,000 ft by Friday. That’s a huge short-term mass load on an already stressed forearc and volcanic edifice.
→ Translation: high confidence in flooding and slides, low confidence in any immediate “big quake trigger.” It’s hydrologic hazard first, tectonic stress background.

YAKUTAT, ALASKA
– M5.8 at ~3 mi depth north of Yakutat, followed by a tight swarm of M2.9–3.5s.
– Sits on the Yakutat microplate collision front, where 1899 M8+ and 1958 M7.7 Lituya Bay hit.
→ Pattern matches a shallow tectonic adjustment and aftershock sequence, not runaway escalation right now. But this corridor remains one of the most likely future M7+ candidates on the North Pacific rim.

ASIA – CYCLONES + FLOODS
– Cyclones Ditwah (Sri Lanka) and Senyar (Sumatra/Malaysia) produced some of the deadliest recent weather disasters in the region. ~1,750 dead, many missing.
– Attribution work: 5-day heavy rain intensity up 28–160% in the Senyar region; in Sri Lanka heavy-rain periods now 9–50% more intense. Flood depths locally 14–15 ft.
→ Warmer oceans + monsoon + cyclones = repeated extreme loading and unloading of water and sediment right over the Sunda subduction system.

RING OF FIRE – JAPAN / FIJI / PHILIPPINES
– M7.6 Aomori, Japan: ~40–45 km deep, ~30 s rupture, classic subduction thrust with several meters of slip. Aftershocks ongoing offshore Honshu.
– Ongoing M4–5 activity around Taiwan, Philippines, Vanuatu–Fiji, plus deep focus quakes in the Tonga–Fiji sink zone.
→ This is a busy but still “within envelope” arc response, consistent with a stressed system that has not crossed into rupture phase.

CDIGR INTERPRETATION
– Core–mantle torque + polar drift are biasing mass and heat toward the Siberia/Arctic side.
– The planet is rebalancing by:
• deep down-welling in the Fiji–Tonga gravity sink
• collision and uplift in Alaska/Yakutat and Japan
• hydrologic extremes over subduction margins (PNW, Sri Lanka, Sumatra).
– None of this guarantees a specific date or location for a mega-quake. It shows where the pressure is concentrating and how fast the envelope is tightening.

Bottom line: we’re still in the loading and redistribution phase, not the 2027–2030 rupture window. The signal is real. The timing is still probabilistic.

* A man walks down a mud-covered street in Aceh Tamiang in Indonesia after flood waters receded.
